unit: Spring 2: Transport, the periodic table and waves
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y10 lesson 115 (30-mark mixed paper with mark scheme (portal))
intro: Mixed paper: 30 marks. Answer every question; show your working. The marks are in brackets.

questions.a: B) Phloem. Phloem carries sucrose and amino acids; xylem carries water and ions.
B) Lymphocyte. Lymphocytes make antibodies; phagocytes engulf pathogens.
B) Breathing out carbon dioxide. CO₂ is a waste product of respiration, made by cells.

questions.q: In the hand-withdrawal reflex, the effector is...
questions.a: C) The muscle. Effectors carry out the response: the muscle contracts.
B) Insulin. Insulin causes cells to take up glucose and the liver to store it as glycogen.

questions.q: Shivering helps warm the body because...
options: Muscles contract, respiring and releasing heat
questions.a: A) Muscles contract, respiring and releasing heat. Muscle contraction needs respiration, which releases energy as heat.

questions.q: Celery practical at home with an adult (celery in coloured water for 24 h, cut across, magnifier). Draw the cross-section and label xylem; answer: 'Explain your observations.'
questions.a: Coloured dots in a ring (1); these are xylem vessels (1); water and dye moved up the xylem from the base (1)
questions.model: Teacher shows a cut celery stem on camera and labels the first coloured dot 'xylem vessel'.

questions.q: Compare transport in xylem and phloem.
questions.a: Xylem carries water and ions; phloem carries sucrose and amino acids (1); xylem one direction, phloem both (1); xylem dead hollow cells, phloem living (1)

questions.q: Aphids feed on plant sap from the stem. Which tissue do they pierce, and how could you tell?
Give two ways xylem is adapted to transport water.
questions.a: Hollow with no end walls so water flows freely (1); lignin strengthens walls so they do not collapse (1)
questions.model: Think structure then function. No end walls: continuous tube. Lignin: strong walls. Each linked to how water moves.

questions.q: Name the substances carried in phloem.

questions.a: It carries substances up and down, from sources to sinks

questions.q: Describe how white blood cells protect the body when bacteria enter a cut. Portal response box.
questions.a: Phagocytes move to the bacteria (1), engulf them (1) and digest them with enzymes (1); lymphocytes recognise antigens (1), produce specific antibodies (1), which bind/clump bacteria so they are destroyed (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes the first point: 'Phagocytes are attracted to the bacteria and engulf them.'

questions.q: Explain why people living at high altitude develop more red blood cells.
questions.a: Less oxygen in the air (1); more red cells/haemoglobin carry enough oxygen to tissues (1)

questions.q: Antibiotics kill bacteria but not viruses. Why must the immune system deal with viruses?
questions.a: Antibiotics target bacterial structures viruses lack; antibodies and lymphocytes still recognise viral antigens.

questions.q: Name three substances carried in plasma.
questions.a: Any three: CO₂, digested food (glucose, amino acids), urea, hormones (heat also transported)
Its shape fits only one antigen
